title: A new approach to the Kondo effect: sophomore's dream function and Lee-Yang zeros
abstract: We develop an analytical approach to the Kondo problem based on an effective partition function that generalizes the sophomore's dream integral. The Kondo crossover is represented as a passage through an approximately equidistant ladder of its Lee-Yang zeros in the complex plane, rather than as a singularity on the real axis. Summation over this ladder yields the Gamma function $Γ(α+ T_K/(2 πT))$ as the universal crossover backbone, where the offset $α=1/2$ is fixed by the Friedel sum rule. The Euler-Maclaurin expansion connects the discrete zero structure to the Nozieres Fermi-liquid theory through Bernoulli numbers. A two-cutoff formula provides a compact, essentially one-parameter description of the full crossover in terms of a temperature-space Fano lineshape which is a thermal average of the energy-space Fano resonance observed in STM. Drift corrections are treated. The approach extends to $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ Coqblin-Schrieffer, underscreened and Anderson impurity models, and Kondo lattices.
summary: This paper presents a novel analytical framework for the Kondo effect crossover by mapping the physics onto the distribution of Lee-Yang zeros in the complex plane. It derives the universal crossover backbone using the Gamma function and provides a generalized, compact description applicable to various impurity models. This offers a powerful mathematical tool for understanding quantum impurity scattering beyond standard approximations.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a rigorous analytical theory to describe the full temperature crossover of the Kondo effect, moving beyond existing approximations.
main_result: The crossover backbone is found to be governed by the Gamma function $\Gamma(\alpha + T_K/(2 \pi T))$, and the method provides a compact, one-parameter description via a Fano lineshape.
method: The approach utilizes an effective partition function generalizing the sophomore's dream integral, modeling the crossover via the passage through an equidistant ladder of Lee-Yang zeros in the complex plane.
model_or_system: The primary system is the Kondo model, extended to $\mathrm{SU}(N)$ and including underscreened and Anderson impurity models. The analysis focuses on the temperature dependence of the effective coupling constant.
key_observables: Resistivity ratio ($ho_{NS}/ho_u$), free energy $F(T)$, and the scattering phase shift $\delta(T)$.
important_parameters: Kondo temperature ($T_K$), Friedel sum rule offset ($\alpha=1/2$), and the temperature-dependent trajectory $t(T)$.
main_assumptions: The partition function is treated as an effective approximation, and the crossover is characterized by the structure of Lee-Yang zeros rather than a real-axis singularity.
figures_summary: Figure 1 compares the calculated relative resistivity $ho(T)/ho_u$ using a derived formula against the standard Hamann approximation.
paper_structure: The paper builds from defining the effective partition function and relating the crossover to Lee-Yang zeros, deriving the universal Gamma function backbone, connecting this to Fermi-liquid theory via Euler-Maclaurin, and finally extending the formalism to various impurity models and lattice systems.
why_interesting: The rigorous mathematical machinery involving complex zeros (Lee-Yang zeros) to describe a crossover phenomenon is highly sophisticated and applicable to understanding quantum critical points or spectral features in strongly correlated systems, which is relevant to AMO physics when considering impurity coupling.
